FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: cubes of {0_adj} marinated in oil, {1_plur} and {2_plur}, threaded on small skewers and grilled fast. The name means simply little skewer.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} drained overnight in a cloth, mixed with {1_plur} grated and wrung out — otherwise the water ruins it all — and raw {2_plur}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cooked until they crush under a finger, ground with a {1_adj} paste, {2_plur} and iced water that whitens them and makes them swell.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: stale flatbread, toasted and broken by hand, thrown over {1_coll} and {2_coll} with sumac. Served at the last moment: the bread must still crack.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: mujadara
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {1_coll} cooked together, covered over with {2_adj} fried to an almost black brown. That near-burning is the whole dish; without it there are only lentils.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tabbouleh
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a mountain of herbs chopped by knife, {1_coll} in dice, and only a handful of bulgur. The version in which the grain dominates is an invention from elsewhere.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: avgolemono
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} beaten with {1_plur} and let down ladle by ladle with the scalding broth before going back into it. Poured in all at once, they curdle and the dish is lost.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: stifado
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} braised with as much whole {1_adj} as meat, with {2_plur} and cinnamon. The onions are not an aromatic here: they are half the dish.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: labneh
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} salted and hung in a cloth for a whole day, until it can be spread, hollowed into a well of {1_adj} oil and dusted with {2_adj}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: shish taouk
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} marinated in {1_plur} and {2_plur}, grilled on skewers and served with a garlic emulsion so dense that it holds on the spoon.
